variants.candidate: You do not need a fresh beginning every time progress gets quiet. Keep a weekly note of what your current work has gained. Give one useful effort a regular place on the calendar. Check the result each month before adding another commitment. Write down the next small task.
variants.original: Growing things still need a gardener’s ruthlessness. Once a season, walk the whole field: feed what is fruiting, and let one dead project go without guilt. Keep the daily habits exactly as they are. And claim the growth out loud, raise the price, take the credit, sooner than feels polite.

variants.candidate: Ease is a gift right up until it dodges every hard thing. Pick one piece of what you make and finish it to done, not to pleasant. Say the awkward true sentence once a week, to the person it belongs to. Comfort that never risks anything eventually feeds no one.
